title: Lower the three-cycle Boolean-cut ceiling to 17/3 (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

A scoped proof, conditional on the cited spectral inequality in #5063, lowers the register-independent three-cycle permutation-cut ceiling to `17t/3`. Final rounding therefore certifies at most 17 calls for three targets. This method cannot prove the direct `6t` tariff already at `t = 3`.

```diff
- ceiling: ((27 + 9 sqrt(2))/7) t; obstruction starts at four targets
+ ceiling: (17/3) t; obstruction starts at three targets
```

The new step uses the 168-element regular action, the order-three crossing cap `k <= 56`, the even six-CNOT boundary, and a rational gap. Orbit lifting extends it to every finite action, address dimension, target triple/orientation and dirty-register count in the stated formal model. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Krzysztof Wojt's spectral theorem and James Reed's cut formulas retain their credit; neither is replayed or claimed as new.

## Evidence

- All 14,364 scalar pairs checked exactly. The maximum allowed by the retained scalar constraints is `17/3`, at `(k,d) = (17,18), (34,36), (51,54)`. These are arithmetic witnesses, not asserted realizable cuts.
- All 128 seven-point subsets and their regular lifts checked for fiber multiplicity, crossing transport, parity and the order-three cap. Three essential-hypothesis controls reject the false statements.
- Registered normal and optimized warning-as-error checks pass on CPython 3.12.15, Darwin 27.0.0 arm64. Each direct check took 0.03–0.04 seconds; the complete package replay took 0.29 seconds.
- `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` with source-history ancestry pass at `1ac2f221a987b2cd0a5154e762ecad03b854eb60`. The generated stdout report binds the five package files by SHA-256.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-cycle-boolean-rounding
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/three-cycle-boolean-rounding/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/three-cycle-boolean-rounding/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/three-cycle-boolean-rounding --check-source-history
```

Any standard-library CPython 3.12 interpreter can replace the displayed local interpreter path.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The mathematical corollary depends on #5063 at `9ad4c47068f900fa1619191292539adcced0d638`. Its spectral certificate is a cited external theorem, not a runtime input or independently verified premise here. Local PASS checks the new arithmetic and lifting step. The exact Boolean-cut optimum, attainability of `17/3`, actual three-target word minimum, independent human/formal-kernel review, native realization, supplier/compiler/precision/storage admission and selected-construction cold replay remain outside this result. There is no new kappa or frontier change.

## Open next questions

1. Determine the exact Boolean-cut optimum on the 168-element regular action using a rigorously certified primal/dual pair and complete optimality argument. No attaining cut or global Boolean certificate is provided.
2. Decide three-target word additivity with a nonlinear or integer label-count invariant beyond this cut cone. No new invariant or complete three-target word census is provided.

## Related open work

- #5063 studies the same three-cycle permutation-cut quantity. Its spectral ceiling is the cited predecessor; this adds Boolean-integrality rounding and moves the obstruction threshold from four targets to three. It does not recompute its spectral numbers.
